question: What is Edward Jones's advisor attrition rate compared to Merrill's?

claims.text: Edward Jones defines its attrition metric as the annualized number of financial advisors that left or retired from the Partnership during the period compared to the total number of financial advisors as of period end (10-Q for the quarter ended 2025-09-26, published 2025-11-07).
In its second-quarter 2025 10-Q (published 2025-08-08), Edward Jones said financial advisor attrition increased to 6.4%, primarily due to an increase in retirements, consistent with industry trends.

In its third-quarter 2025 10-Q (published 2025-11-07), Edward Jones reported financial advisor attrition of 6.1% versus 4.7% in the third quarter of 2024, and 6.0% for the nine months versus 5.1% a year earlier. It attributed the quarter to a variety of factors, including a rise in departures among advisors with tenure of five years or less.

The Edward Jones 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) names attrition as a risk. It states there is no assurance the Partnership can grow, retain, develop and support its financial advisors, and no assurance that past attrition rates will not increase. It says lower Firm profitability and revenue could increase attrition. It also says advisor attrition could rise if product offerings or the employment model do not meet advisor expectations.

On the 2Q26 earnings call (2026-07-14), Bank of America's CFO, discussing the Merrill growth guide, said adviser attrition is now at near historic lows. No numeric Merrill attrition rate is given in the evidence.

Edward Jones's 10-Q for the second quarter of 2025 (published 2025-08-08) shows 20,309 financial advisors at period end versus 19,589 a year earlier (+4%). The 10-Q for the third quarter of 2025 (published 2025-11-07) says the Partnership ended the quarter with 20,429 financial advisors.

The Edward Jones 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) says the Partnership relies heavily on referrals from its current financial advisors to recruit new advisors. It says it has been, and may continue to be, more difficult to attract qualified applicants in volatile markets, and that new advisors may struggle to build their businesses.

On the 2Q25 call (2025-07-16), Bank of America's CFO said the firm continued to add financial advisors to the sales force in Merrill and the Private Bank through its training program and experienced hiring. He said about one-third of net new households in Q2 were added by newly trained advisors.

On the 4Q25 call (2026-01-14), the CFO said Merrill FAs see the value of the franchise and the firm is picking up recruiting of experienced advisors. He described this as not an enormous part of the strategy, alongside a training program.

On the 1Q26 call (2026-04-15), the CFO said the firm continues to attract talent across both new and experienced advisers. On the 3Q26 call (2026-10-14), he said Merrill results reflect the firm's ability to attract clients and experienced advisers to the platform.

adjacent.text: Bank of America's 4Q23 supplement (published 2024-01-12) shows total wealth advisors at period end of 18,916 (4Q23), 19,130 (3Q23), 19,099 (2Q23) and 19,243 (1Q23), against 19,273 at year-end 2022. It says the count includes advisors across all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking.
adjacent.differs_because: Net advisor headcount change is not attrition: it nets hires against departures. This is also an older (2023), wider-scope count that includes GWIM and Consumer Banking, not Merrill alone.

adjacent.text: Bank of America's November 2025 investor-day deck (published 2025-11-05) shows more than 15K wealth advisors for Merrill | Private Bank.
adjacent.differs_because: Net advisor headcount change is not attrition: it nets hires against departures. This is a single point-in-time count for Merrill plus the Private Bank, not Merrill alone, and it is not a change figure.

gaps.what: Neither firm discloses advisor attrition on a comparable basis. Edward Jones publishes a quarterly annualized attrition percentage, but Merrill discloses no numeric attrition rate (only the qualitative 'near historic lows'), so no like-for-like comparison is possible.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America/Merrill investor-day or 10-K human-capital disclosure; industry recruiter data (e.g., Cerulli, Financial Planning)

gaps.what: Edward Jones's attrition figures for the first and second quarters of 2026 are not in the evidence provided. The latest figure available is 6.1% for 3Q25.
gaps.suggested_source: Edward Jones 10-Q MD&A key metrics table, Q1 and Q2 2026

gaps.what: Merrill does not disclose advisor headcount change, retention rate or advisor recruiting numbers on a standalone basis in the evidence provided.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America quarterly earnings supplement (current advisor headcount) or Merrill investor-day materials
